title.en: Winged creature flight cycle and banking turns

summary: Build a flier whose wing cycle, banking and heading come from one motion state instead of three unrelated animations.
objective: Create a flying creature that flaps, glides and banks into turns, with the wing cycle driven by its actual motion.
intent_signals: Make a flying creature that turns believably.
Build a wing flap cycle that responds to speed rather than looping at a fixed rate.
example_prompts: Create a flying creature with flap, glide and banking turns driven by its motion state.
Build a bird-like flier that circles a landmark and lands on it.
negative_signals: Not an aerodynamic flight model: no lift, drag or stall is computed.
not_for: Not an aerodynamic flight model: no lift, drag or stall is computed.

entities.name: Wing structure
entities.guidance: Build the wing as a jointed arm with membrane or feather layers driven by joint angles, so folding and extension are structural rather than a scale change.

entities.name: Body and tail
entities.guidance: Give the body a spine chain and a steering tail, so banking involves the whole creature rather than only the wings.

entities.name: Flight state
entities.guidance: Hold speed, heading, bank angle and flap phase as one state, since every visible motion should be derived from it.

state_contract.model: Flight state with position, speed, heading, bank angle and flap phase; the wing cycle rate is derived from speed and climb demand, and bank angle is derived from turn rate. Landing is a state transition with a stated approach.
state_contract.authority: The flight state is authoritative. Wing pose, tail deflection and body roll are all derived from it, so an animation that plays while the state is idle is a defect.
actions: Steer the creature along a path or toward a target.
Command a landing on a marked perch.

invariants: Under the coordinated-flight rule this scene chooses, bank angle follows the commanded turn rate with a declared lag, so roll-in and roll-out legitimately show bank while the heading is still changing. Glide, landing approach and idle are separate states with their own pose rules.
In flapping flight the cycle rate follows speed and climb demand; in glide and idle the flap phase is held at a declared pose rather than continuing to advance.

Landing uses a foot-to-support alignment rule: the feet are placed on the perch surface and the flight state ends only then, since capsule contact alone does not establish that the feet are on the perch.
motion_guidance: Use anticipation before the first downstroke and follow-through in the wing tips, and offset the tail so it does not move in lockstep with the wings.
Blend between flapping and gliding through pose targets rather than cross-fading two clips.
known_limits: Authored motion: nothing here predicts real flight performance or energy cost.
Wing membranes are driven by joints; no cloth or feather simulation is implied.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

object_craft.structure: Shoulder, elbow and wrist joints with primaries or membrane panels attached along the forearm and hand, and visible attachment at the body.
object_craft.material: Layered surfaces with slight translucency at membrane edges; feather or membrane detail should read as geometry at silhouette scale.
object_craft.articulation: Wing pose is driven by the flap phase and by the fold parameter used for gliding and perching.

object_craft.structure: Spine chain with a heavier chest mass and a tail that can fan and twist.
object_craft.material: Matte body with a distinct surface treatment on the underside so bank angle is legible against the sky.
object_craft.articulation: Roll is applied to the spine root; the tail lags the body by a short offset.

physical_contract.scope: Authored flight steering with bounded acceleration and turn rate; no aerodynamics or collision response beyond landing contact.
colliders: Body capsule for perch contact and obstacle blocking.
driving: Bounded acceleration, climb rate and turn rate; flap rate derived from speed and climb demand.
contact: Perch landing places feet on the support surface and stops motion.
checks: For the authored coordinated-flight state, bank follows the declared turn signal with the stated response lag; evaluate roll-in, roll-out, glide, landing and idle under their own state rules.
Feet contact the perch on landing without interpenetration.

creative_affordances: The creature can be avian, chiropteran or invented, as long as the wing arm remains structurally readable.
Flight personality is a design lever: heavy slow beats or quick nervous flicks both work with the same state model.
